historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_fy21_to_fy26e_cagr (spans the full FY2023-24 downcycle and the FY2025-26 upcycle, including Spirent). Equity CAGR (12.3%) rejected as the anchor: it is inflated by buybacks running below earnings and by $2.0B of acquisition-funded asset growth, and diverges >30% from revenue (5.0%) and EPS (8.0%).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 12.3% vs revenue 5.0% / EPS 8.0% -- divergence >30%. Equity growth reflects retained earnings and M&A, not organic scale. Base 10-year revenue CAGR is set at ~5.3%, between the 5-year revenue CAGR and the through-cycle FY21-FY26E CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are computed on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding - interest income): FY2020 $742M -> FY2025 $964M (5.4%/yr) and FY2022 $743M -> FY2025 $964M (9.1%/yr). Both sit below the reported-FCF CAGRs (7.3% / 10.1%): SBC rose from $93M to $176M and interest income from $11M to $102M over FY2020-25, so ~2pp/yr of reported FCF growth was paid for in stock or earned on the cash pile rather than by the operating business. All figures use audited FY2025 as the endpoint; FY2026E is an estimate and is used only as the FY0 anchor. Series: owner FCF FY2019 747, FY2020 742, FY2021 988, FY2022 743, FY2023 924, FY2024 641, FY2025 964.

scenario_narratives.base: One more strong year on backlog (FY2027 +14%), normalisation (FY2028 +7%), an explicit digestion year (FY2029 -3%, pre-SBC EBITDA margin 30.5%), then mid-single-digit compounding to a 32.5% through-cycle margin. The axes are (1) how long the AI data-center test cycle runs before hyperscalers digest, (2) whether defense modernisation and the 6G inflection (guided 1H FY2028) fill the gap, and (3) whether the software/recurring mix (~29% ARR) keeps the trough margin above the last cycle's 25%.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI infrastructure test demand (1.6T/3.2T Ethernet, co-packaged optics, silicon photonics) is multi-year rather than a spike; 6G R&D lands on schedule; defense and space stay double-digit. No digestion year, 35% pre-SBC EBITDA margin, SBC falls toward 3.2% of revenue, tax holds at 17%. ~7.8% 10-year revenue CAGR.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI capex digestion from FY2028 plus a China export-control/tariff shock: two down years (-8%, -6%), trough margin 26%, recovery only to the last cycle's 28.5% average, 20% cash tax, 2.5% terminal growth. ~1.8% 10-year revenue CAGR. Cash generation stays positive throughout; this is a de-rating path, not a solvency path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the operating business on fully-SBC-charged owner FCF through a full cycle, discounted at a single USD WACC, with the cycle expressed in the scenario paths and weights rather than the discount rate. The FY2026E anchor is a peak (Spirent-boosted +32% revenue, non-GAAP operating margin 33% above target), so no scenario extrapolates it: the base includes a digestion year and settles at a through-cycle margin. The valuation deliberately does not credit unfunded M&A (Ixia, ESI, Spirent contributed ~3pp/yr of the last decade's revenue CAGR and were paid for in cash that this model treats as retained by shareholders). The house intrinsic value is compared with the street basis (SBC as non-cash) via band_position; the required-return table shows what return today's price implies on the base path.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle timing: if the AI data-center test cycle runs two years longer than the base path assumes, FY2028-29 revenue is 15-20% above the base and the value moves toward the bull case; if hyperscalers digest in FY2027, the base overstates near-term FCF.
Margin durability: the 32.5% through-cycle pre-SBC EBITDA margin is above the last cycle's average; if the trough repeats FY2024's 25%, value falls toward the bear case.
China / export controls / tariffs: a high-single-digit revenue exposure that policy can remove abruptly.
Terminal value share: Gordon growth binds in all scenarios; ~55-60% of EV sits in the terminal, so each 1pp of WACC moves value ~15%.
Tax: cash taxes run ~10% of pre-tax income today; the ramp to 19% is a judgment on Pillar Two and the Singapore incentive; holding 14% for a decade would add ~5% to value.
Anchor estimate: FY0 revenue and FCF are FY2026E (9M actuals + Q4 guidance) and should be replaced with the FY2026 10-K figures in December 2026.
The DuckDB/CSV total_debt (3,217) double-counts the $700M current portion; the model uses 2,517 from XBRL. If the CSV is corrected the net-debt input should be re-checked.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average 173.0m from the Q3 FY2026 10-Q (quarter to 2026-07-31) dilutive-securities table; cover-page basic count 170.24m at 2026-08-27. Held FLAT because SBC (incl. withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count. Buybacks ($517M in 9M FY2026) are the cash mechanism keeping the count flat and are value-neutral here.
inputs.debt_note: Total debt 2,517 = LongTermDebtNoncurrent 1,817 + current portion 700 (senior notes due Apr-2027), per XBRL at 2026-07-31. The DuckDB/CSV total_debt of 3,217 double-counts the current portion (LongTermDebt 2,517 already includes it); the CSV figure is NOT used here. Operating lease liabilities (~$0.2B) excluded: leases are expensed in opex under ASC 842 (treatment B).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026E interest income ~$72M (9M: $54M) is NOT stripped: net cash is only $88M against a ~$1.5B owner-FCF base, far below the 1x materiality threshold, and it is broadly offset by ~$105M/yr of interest expense on the $2.5B of notes. Reported FCF is therefore a slightly levered figure; the forward component build is unlevered by construction.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL: ShareBasedCompensation 9M FY2026 $181M (CSV basis $182M) annualised to ~$240M; PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 9M FY2026 $41M, FY2026E $43M (withholding is front-loaded in Q1; FY2025 was $39M on 9M $38M). No company-published combined figure, so the two lines are summed. FY2025 actual: SBC $176M + withholding $39M = $215M on reported FCF $1,281M.
inputs.buyback_note: 9M FY2026 repurchases $517M (FY2025 $375M, FY2024 $439M); new $1.5B authorisation Nov-2025. Active repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.fy0_note: FY2026 ends 31-Oct-2026. FY0 = 9M actuals (revenue $5,163M; GAAP operating income $1,116M; reported FCF $1,282M) plus Q4 at the guidance midpoint ($1.93-1.95B revenue, non-GAAP EPS $3.34-3.40; ~26.5% GAAP operating margin assumed). Company guides ~32% FY2026 revenue growth, which ties to $7,100M. FY2025 audited actuals for reference: revenue $5,375M, reported FCF $1,281M, owner FCF $1,066M (before interest strip).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: 10-year UST ~4.2% (Sep-2026), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~9.7%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (2027/2029/2032/2035 senior notes) -> ~3.7% after tax; weights ~96% equity / 4% debt at market -> WACC ~9.5%. The SAME 9.5% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, AI-capex digestion and China/export-control risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights (adaptations rule f), not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. US GAAP ASC 842 operating lease cost (~$67M/yr FY2026E) is already inside GAAP operating expense, hence inside the EBITDA margin path; operating lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. No separate lease_cost_pct_path is needed.
inputs.ebitda_basis_note: ebitda_margin_path is pre-SBC EBITDA on a GAAP cost basis: GAAP operating income + depreciation + amortisation of intangibles + SBC. FY2026E: 1,630 + 155 + 261 + 240 = 2,286 = 32.2% of revenue. Acquisition, integration and restructuring costs that the company excludes from non-GAAP (Q3 FY2026 non-GAAP operating margin 33.2% vs GAAP 25.0%) are treated as recurring for a serial acquirer (Ixia 2017, ESI 2023-24, Spirent 2025). History on the same basis: FY2023 peak ~32.4%, FY2024 trough ~24.9%, FY2025 ~24.6% (Spirent deal costs), so 32-33% is a peak-cycle margin and the base path spends its digestion year at 30.5%.
inputs.da_basis_note: da_pct_path carries depreciation (~2.2% of revenue, FY2026E $155M) plus a small allowance for deductible amortisation only. Acquired-intangible amortisation (~$261M, 3.7% of revenue in FY2026E, mostly Spirent) is deliberately EXCLUDED: in this engine D&A affects only the cash-tax base, and Spirent was a share purchase whose intangibles are not tax-deductible. Including it would book a tax shield the company does not get. The excluded amortisation is non-cash and has no reinvestment requirement, so FCF is unaffected. Capex path (~2.2-2.6%) is set to converge with depreciation so the terminal year is at steady state.
inputs.wc_note: Working capital consumes cash on growth: receivables (~$1.2B) + inventory (~$1.0B) exceed payables + deferred revenue (~$0.7B). wc_capture_pct is negative (-10% of the YoY revenue change in base/bull, -8% in bear); it returns cash in the down years.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (owner_fcf_dcf_component), 10-year explicit horizon FY2027-FY2036, end-of-year discounting, TV = max(0, min(Gordon, cap x FCF_N)). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (operating company, cyclical) -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (cyclical: risk charged once). Keysight is a profitable electronic test & measurement OEM with ~37% software/services revenue; its cash flow statement means what the engine assumes, so no non-FCF model applies. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). Cycle position: this is a PEAK-cycle anchor. FY2026E revenue +32% (Spirent adds ~7-8pp inorganic; organic ~24%), Q3 orders +56%, GAAP operating margin running 25% and non-GAAP 33.2% -- above the long-term target range. The base path therefore takes one more strong year (FY2027 +14% on backlog), a normalising FY2028, an explicit digestion year (FY2029 -3%, margin 30.5%), then mid-single-digit growth fading to 3.5% and a 32.5% through-cycle pre-SBC EBITDA margin (above the FY2019-25 average ~29% because scale and software/recurring mix are structurally higher post-Spirent). Gordon binds the terminal value in every scenario (Gordon multiples 14.6x-17.3x vs caps 15/18/20x). Price is a regular close, not after-hours. Total debt taken from XBRL (2,517), not the CSV's double-counted 3,217.

bear.narrative: Hyperscaler AI capex digests from FY2028 (FY2028 -8%, FY2029 -6%, a repeat of the FY2023-24 downturn but from a higher base), compounded by a China export-control or tariff shock that removes a high-single-digit share of revenue. Deleverage and sticky SBC drop the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 26% at the trough, recovering only to 28.5% -- the FY2019-25 average, i.e. no structural mix benefit. Recovery is at trend 3-5% and terminal growth 2.5%; cash taxes converge on the 20% GAAP rate as the Singapore incentive rolls off under Pillar Two. 10-year revenue CAGR ~1.8%. No solvency risk: net cash today and a 2027 note maturity comfortably covered.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +14%: Q3 FY2026 orders +56% YoY and book-to-bill >1.1 give backlog cover; consensus-style deceleration from the +32% FY2026 pace. FY2028 +7% as AI data-center test spend normalises. FY2029 -3%: explicit digestion year -- test & measurement has had one roughly every 4-5 years (FY2016 flat, FY2020 -2%, FY2024 -9%). FY2030-36 recovery at 6-7% fading to 3.5% (defense modernisation, 6G inflection guided for 1H FY2028, semiconductor complexity, recurring-mix growth). 10-year CAGR ~5.3% vs 5-year history 5.0% and FY21-26E 7.5%.
base.margin_rationale: FY2027-28 at 33.5% pre-SBC EBITDA (GAAP-cost basis): +1.3pp on FY2026E via the 40%+ incremental-margin framework, but capped below the Q3 exit rate because acquisition/restructuring costs recur. Digestion year deleverages to 30.5%, then rebuilds to a 32.5% through-cycle level -- above the FY2019-25 average (~29%) for structural mix reasons, but below the current peak.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax rate on EBIT ramps 14% -> 19%. FY2026E cash taxes (~$190M) run at ~10% of pre-tax income thanks to the Singapore incentive, OBBBA restoration of domestic R&D expensing (July 2025) and Spirent-related deferred items. Pillar Two 15% minimum applies from FY2025 and the company's own non-GAAP rate is 17%; GAAP ETR FY2025 was 19.7%. 19% terminal sits between non-GAAP and GAAP.
base.narrative: Keysight rides the AI data-center / defense / advanced-semiconductor cycle for one more strong year, then normalises through a digestion year and compounds at mid-single digits with a structurally higher through-cycle margin than the last cycle.

bull.narrative: The AI infrastructure build-out proves multi-year (1.6T/3.2T Ethernet, co-packaged optics, silicon photonics), 6G R&D inflects on schedule in FY2028 so there is no digestion year -- only a slow FY2029 (+4%) -- and defense/space demand stays double-digit. Incremental margins hold above 40%, lifting the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 35% (non-GAAP operating margin ~36%), with the software/recurring mix compressing SBC to 3.2% of revenue and the tax rate holding at the company's 17% non-GAAP rate. 10-year revenue CAGR ~7.8%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 25/50/25. Bull weight cut because the bull case needs three independent things to go right at once -- a multi-year AI test cycle, an on-time 6G inflection, and no China/export-control disruption -- and it is being priced from a peak-cycle anchor (orders +56%, margins above the long-term target range). Bear weight raised to 25% because the business is demonstrably cyclical (FY2024 revenue -9%, GAAP operating margin 16.7%) and the bear axis (AI capex digestion + China) is a live macro risk rated 'high' in the Analysis; not higher because the balance sheet is net cash with no refinancing or going-concern exposure, so the bear is a de-rating, not a survival, scenario.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
